rationale: Canvas2D's initial textBaseline is alphabetic, but the JS shim, the widget-bridge registrar and CanvasWidget::paint all defaulted to top, so browser-authored canvas code that never assigns ctx.textBaseline had every string drawn one full ascent below the y it passed -- a caption written just above a plot landed inside it. This change makes alphabetic the default on all three surfaces, appends alphabetic/hanging/ideographic to canvas::TextBaseline, and widens the bridge's wire mapping accordingly. That is deliberately a change in rendered output, not a no-op: canvas content that had been laid out against the old top default will now draw text higher by one ascent. That is the fix, and it is stated here rather than claimed away. The hanging and ideographic placements are approximations and are unmeasured: TextMetrics exposes no BASE-table metric, so ideographic shares the descent line with bottom and hanging uses the conventional 0.8x ascent. Neither has been compared pixel-for-pixel against a browser, and both should be treated as unverified against a reference engine. Separately, the CSS paint lane no longer coerces an absent or unparseable opacity to 0; CSS's initial value is 1, and the old coercion made a pseudo-class restore silently stop a widget painting while its rect, visibility and clip box stayed intact, which reads as a renderer fault rather than a style reset. The render-assets-and-backends surface touched is core/canvas and core/view only: an additive enum in the public canvas header, with the existing top/middle/bottom wire codes 0/1/2 left at their values, plus the two web-compat JS shim files, CanvasWidget::paint and the canvas2d bridge registrar. No renderer or GPU backend code, no Skia pin, no font or asset changes, and no harness or fixture changes. Registered watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.
